title: Microsoft 365 admin center: manage Viva feature access policies on a page as well as in PowerShell
summary: The briefing passes: Microsoft documentation supports the policy controls, PowerShell calls, licensing requirements and limits. It accurately reports the stale roadmap status and conflicting People Skills guidance, without inventing a default for the new interface.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Feature access policies enable or disable Viva features for users, groups or the whole tenant.
claims.quote: Policies are used to restrict or grant access to the specified feature for specific users, groups, or the entire tenant.

claims.claim: The roadmap states that these policies previously could only be managed using PowerShell cmdlets.
claims.quote: Previously, these policies could only be managed with Microsoft PowerShell cmdlets.

claims.where: title; summary; What's changing; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The roadmap plans management of the same access policies through either the admin centre or PowerShell.
claims.quote: After this rollout, admins can choose to use either Microsoft 365 admin center or PowerShell to manage feature access.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Existing policies persist and can be managed in both places, according to the roadmap.
claims.quote: Existing policies set for an organization will persist and can be managed in both places.

claims.where: front matter: defaultState; Why it matters; Risk assessment; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Microsoft has not explicitly stated the new interface's default state on arrival.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva feature access management admin center policies licensing default state arrival; Viva feature access admin center default automatically new interface. Read control-access-admin-center, feature-access-management, manage-access-policies and the roadmap; none states a new-interface default.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.model and notes; Cost and licensing; rationale: cost
claims.claim: Policy creation is covered by a supported version of Microsoft 365 or a Viva Suite licence.
claims.quote: Policy creation requires the following elements: A supported version of Microsoft 365 or a Viva Suite license.

claims.where: front matter: licensing.notes; Cost and licensing
claims.claim: The Viva features governed by policies remain subject to their own licensing requirements.
claims.quote: The following table lists the major Microsoft Viva features available across plans. Certain caveats apply. For more information, see the footnotes.

claims.claim: Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app > feature > Access setting reaches the feature enablement control in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: select Viva from the settings menu. Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. Select Create a policy. Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy. Select the Access setting option

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId <ModuleId> -FeatureId <FeatureId> -Name <policy name> -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone creates a tenant-wide policy disabling the feature.
claims.quote: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -Name DisableFeatureForAll -IsFeatureEnabled $false -Everyone

claims.claim: -IsUserControlEnabled $true lets users opt out where the feature supports admin-controlled user controls.
claims.quote: $true: User control is enabled by the policy. Users can opt out of the feature. Only features that allow admins to enable and disable user controls by policy can use this parameter.

claims.claim: IsUserControlEnabled requires module version 3.3.0-Preview1 or later.
claims.quote: This parameter is available in module version 3.3.0-Preview1 or later.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Scope: Limits; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Only one tenant-wide policy per feature is supported, in addition to user/group policies.
claims.quote: You can assign one additional policy per feature to the entire tenant by using the -Everyone parameter

claims.claim: Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > Create a policy > app > feature > Apply access settings to reaches the policy audience field in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: Select Create a policy. Name the policy and select the app and feature for which you'd like to set the policy. Select Everyone or Specific people and groups under Apply access settings to.

claims.claim: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy with ModuleId, FeatureId, Name, IsFeatureEnabled $false, GroupIds containing group email addresses or object IDs, and UserIds containing UPNs creates a policy for those users and groups.
claims.quote: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -Name UsersAndGroups -IsFeatureEnabled $false -GroupIds group1@contoso.com,group2@contoso.com,57680382-61a5-4378-85ad-f72095d4e9c3 -UserIds user1@contoso.com,user2@contoso.com

claims.where: controls[1].note; Scope: Limits; Governance controls table
claims.claim: At most 10 user/group policies can be assigned per feature.
claims.quote: You can assign a maximum of 10 policies per feature to users and groups.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Scope: Limits; Governance controls table
claims.claim: Each policy may be assigned to at most 20 users or groups in total.
claims.quote: You can specify a maximum of 20 total users or groups (20 users and no groups, 10 users and 10 groups, etc.).

claims.claim: Security group object IDs in GroupIds require module version 3.5.1-Preview2 or later.
claims.quote: In v3.5.1-Preview2 or later of the module, this parameter supports security group object IDs (GUIDs).

claims.claim: Earlier module versions accept only email addresses for GroupIds.
claims.quote: Previous versions of the module accept only email addresses for this parameter.

claims.claim: Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > More actions > Edit policy reaches policy editing in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: From the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Viva from the settings menu. Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. Select the vertical ellipses (More actions) and choose Edit policy.

claims.claim: Update-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId <ModuleId> -FeatureId <FeatureId> -PolicyId <PolicyId> -GroupIds <groups> changes the existing policy's audience to the specified groups.
claims.quote: Update-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -PolicyId xxxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx -GroupIds group1@contoso.com,group2@contoso.com

claims.where: controls[2].note; Risk assessment; Governance guidance; Governance controls table
claims.claim: UserIds, GroupIds or Everyone values in a PowerShell update overwrite the policy's existing users and groups.
claims.quote: Values that you specify for the -UserIds and -GroupIds parameters or the -Everyone parameter overwrite any existing users or groups.

claims.claim: Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access > policy > Delete policy reaches policy deletion in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: From the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Viva from the settings menu. Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. Select the policy you'd like to delete. Select Delete policy.

claims.claim: Remove-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId <ModuleId> -FeatureId <FeatureId> -PolicyId <PolicyId> deletes the specified access policy.
claims.quote: Use the Remove-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy cmdlet to delete an access policy. Remove-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId VivaInsights -FeatureId Reflection -PolicyId xxxxxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxx-xxxxxxxxxxxx

claims.claim: Get-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy provides the policy ID needed for deletion.
claims.quote: This cmdlet provides details about the policies, including the policy's identifier, name, and creation date.

claims.claim: The admin-centre Access setting offers On or Off to enable or disable a feature.
claims.quote: Select the Access setting option and choose On or Off to enable or disable the feature.

claims.claim: Only some features allow users to opt out.
claims.quote: Only some features have the controls available for admins to provide users with the option to opt out.

claims.claim: The UI can apply a policy to Everyone or Specific people and groups.
claims.quote: Select Everyone or Specific people and groups under Apply access settings to. If you didn't select Everyone, add the specific people and groups you want to apply the policy to.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Settings > Viva > Settings > Manage feature access is the page listing existing policies, which can be opened to view details.
claims.quote: From the Microsoft 365 admin center, select Viva from the settings menu. Select the Settings tab and select Manage feature access. Select the policy name to view the details.

claims.claim: Learn documents the admin-centre page as usable even though the supplied roadmap still says In development.
claims.quote: you can create and update policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited admin-centre page says People Skills policies can only be created with PowerShell.
claims.quote: Policies for People Skills can only be created via PowerShell at this time. You cannot use the interface in Microsoft 365 admin center to create policies for People Skills features.

claims.where: What's changing; Governance guidance; Open questions
claims.claim: The cited PowerShell page instead says People Skills policies can be created and managed in either the admin centre or PowerShell.
claims.quote: You can create and manage People Skills feature access policies in the Microsoft 365 admin center or by using PowerShell.

claims.claim: Exchange Online PowerShell version 3.2.0 or later is required for the policy cmdlets.
claims.quote: This cmdlet is available only in the Exchange Online PowerShell module version 3.2.0 or later.

claims.claim: Non-mail-enabled groups require Exchange PowerShell version 3.5.1 or later.
claims.quote: If you need to use non-mail-enabled groups you must have access to Exchange PowerShell version 3.5.1 or later.

claims.claim: Soft-disable policies require Exchange PowerShell version 3.8.0 or later.
claims.quote: If you need to setup policies with the user opted-out by default (soft-disable), you must have access to Exchange PowerShell version 3.8.0 or later.

claims.where: controls[0].note; Why it matters; Risk assessment; Scope
claims.claim: The required feature-management role is specified per feature in the Who can manage access column.
claims.quote: Admins with correct permissions in the Microsoft 365 admin center or in PowerShell can create and manage access policies. For more information, see the Who can manage access column in the following feature table.

claims.claim: Insights admin can manage Reflection access.
claims.quote: | Reflection | No | Insights admin | Viva Insights |

claims.claim: Viva Pulse admin manages the listed Pulse feature controls.
claims.quote: | Pulse | Customization | No | Viva Pulse admin | Viva Pulse |

claims.claim: Global admin is listed for several Viva Insights features.
claims.quote: | Copilot in Viva Insights | No | Global admin** | Viva Insights |

claims.claim: The policy cmdlet references require Global Administrators membership or the roles assigned at feature level.
claims.quote: Currently, you need to be a member of the Global Administrators role or the roles that have been assigned at the feature level to run this cmdlet.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: User/group policies outrank the organisation-wide setting and can allow access when it is turned off organisation-wide.
claims.quote: Custom policies take precedence over your org-wide settings. For example, if you have organization-wide access turned off, a custom policy could still allow access for specific users or groups.

claims.claim: The organisational setting applies where no custom user/group policy applies.
claims.quote: If there are no custom policies set for a user or group, the organizational setting will apply.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Access-policy changes take effect within 24 hours except for feature-specific exceptions.
claims.quote: Changes to access policies take effect for the user within 24 hours, unless noted for a specific feature.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Copilot in Viva Engage policy changes may take up to 48 hours.
claims.quote: Changes for Copilot in Viva Engage might take up to 48 hours.

claims.claim: Changing Access setting to On or Off on a policy offering user opt-out resets the user's opt-out preference.
claims.quote: When you have a policy enabled with the option for users to opt out of a feature, and then you change the Access setting to on or off, the ability for users to opt out is removed. In this case, a user's opt out preference is not preserved and is reset to the default state.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Multiple access-setting changes within 24 hours may prevent the preference reset.
claims.quote: if there are multiple changes to access settings within a 24-hour period, the user's preference may not reset to the default state.

claims.claim: The published policy-creation requirements name no separate price or meter for managing policies on the new page.
claims.quote: Searched: Viva feature access management policy admin center pricing meter license charge. Read Requirements in manage-access-policies and feature-access-management, control-access-admin-center and the Viva service description; no separate policy-management price or meter is specified.

claims.claim: Viva Insights admin is among the roles permitted to manage particular listed features.
claims.quote: | Analyst Report Publish | No | Viva Insights admin | Viva Insights |

claims.claim: Engage admin manages AI Summarization access.
claims.quote: | AI Summarization | Yes | Engage admin | Viva Engage |

claims.claim: Goals admin manages Copilot in Viva Goals access.
claims.quote: | Goals | Copilot in Viva Goals | No | Goals admin | Viva Goals |

claims.claim: Knowledge admin manages the listed People Skills features.
claims.quote: | People Skills | Skills Inferencing | Yes__*__ | Knowledge admin | People Skills |

claims.claim: Learn's feature table covers Viva Engage, Glint, Goals, Insights, Pulse and People Skills features.
claims.quote: Viva Engage; Glint; Goals; Insights; Pulse; People Skills

claims.claim: The settings also apply to Agent 365 Business Analytics (Frontier preview) where applicable.
claims.quote: The settings described below also apply to Agent 365 Business Analytics (Frontier preview) where applicable.

claims.claim: Policy names must be unique.
claims.quote: Policy names must be unique.

claims.claim: Learn says these access controls are not available in GCC-High.
claims.quote: The access controls described in this document aren't available in GCC-High or DoD.

claims.claim: Learn says these access controls are not available in DoD.
claims.quote: The access controls described in this document aren't available in GCC-High or DoD.

claims.claim: Learn directs GCC administrators to the specific app documentation for availability.
claims.quote: For GCC (Government Community Cloud), see the documentation for your specific app for availability.

claims.claim: Policy creation requires user accounts created in or synchronised to Microsoft Entra ID.
claims.quote: User accounts created in or synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID

claims.claim: Supported group types are Microsoft 365 groups, Microsoft Entra security groups and distribution groups, with the stated Entra creation or synchronisation prerequisite.
claims.quote: Microsoft 365 groups, Microsoft Entra security groups created in or synchronized to Microsoft Entra ID, or distribution groups.

claims.claim: Each user has one effective policy per feature.
claims.quote: A user has one effective policy for each feature.

claims.claim: The tenant policy outranks the feature default.
claims.quote: Policy Scope Levels (Most to Least Restrictive): User or Group Policies; Tenant Policy; Defaults

claims.claim: Within a policy scope level, the most restrictive enablement policy wins.
claims.quote: The most restrictive Policy Scope Level takes precedence first. Then within a single Policy Scope Level, the most restrictive Enablement Policy takes precedence.

claims.claim: Some features support only tenant-wide policies.
claims.quote: Some features only support policies that apply to the entire tenant, not specific users or groups.

claims.claim: Get-VivaModuleFeature provides the supported policy scopes for a feature.
claims.quote: You can refer to supported policy scopes for a feature using the Get-VivaModuleFeature cmdlet.

claims.claim: Copilot policies can also be managed through Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
claims.quote: You can manage Copilot policies through Copilot settings in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Copilot policies managed through Copilot settings remain in sync with policies managed through the admin page.
claims.quote: These policies remain in sync with policies managed through the admin page.

claims.claim: VFAM change logs in Microsoft Purview contain the history of policy creation, updates and deletions.
claims.quote: For a history of policy creation, updates, and deletions, see the Viva Feature Access Management (VFAM) change logs for your organization in Microsoft Purview.

claims.claim: PowerShell sets soft disable using -IsFeatureEnabled $true -IsUserControlEnabled $true -IsUserOptedInByDefault $false.
claims.quote: Add-VivaModuleFeaturePolicy -ModuleId PeopleSkills -FeatureId ShowAISkills -Name SoftDisableShowAISkillsPolicy -IsFeatureEnabled $true -IsUserControlEnabled $true -IsUserOptedInByDefault $false -UserIds user1@contoso.com,user2@contoso.com

claims.claim: IsUserOptedInByDefault requires module version 3.8.0-Preview2 or later.
claims.quote: This parameter is available in module version 3.8.0-Preview2 or later.

claims.claim: A soft-disable policy opts users out by default while allowing them to opt in.
claims.quote: Enable the feature by opting out everyone in policy scope by default, while providing users the ability to opt in (soft disable).

claims.claim: The page is an administrator-facing control; users experience changes when policies governing their feature access are changed.
claims.quote: An authorized admin in your tenant can create, assign, and manage access policies from PowerShell. When a user signs in to Microsoft 365, the policy settings are applied, and they only see the features that haven't been disabled.
